summary: Defines MIB objects, in SMIv2 format, for managing IEEE 802.5 Token Ring subnetworks with SNMP. It is a draft standard and updates the earlier RFC 1743.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 1748 defines SNMPv2 objects for managing IEEE 802.5 Token Ring interfaces. The objects report interface state and statistics, and include commands for controlling the interface.

questions: how to manage token ring with snmp
subtitle: The SNMPv2 management objects for IEEE 802.5 Token Ring interfaces.

tldr.problem: Network managers needed a standard SNMPv2 set of objects for checking the state, settings, and errors of IEEE 802.5 Token Ring interfaces.
tldr.mechanism: The dot5 MIB module defines interface and statistics tables, retains an obsolete timer table for compatibility, and identifies tests and chip sets.
tldr.outcome: RFC 1748 replaces RFC 1231 and RFC 1743. It is a Draft Standard and is updated by RFC 1749.

today: RFC 1748 is a Draft Standard published in December 1994. It obsoletes RFC 1231 and RFC 1743, and the unit metadata says RFC 1749 updates it.

sections.title: The dot5 Management Module
sections.content:
This RFC defines a portion of the Management Information Base (MIB) for managing IEEE 802.5 Token Ring subnetworks. It replaces RFC 1231 and uses the SNMPv2 Structure of Management Information.

Each managed object has an object identifier, and an object instance identifies a particular value. The module is named dot5 and is placed under the transmission branch.
sections.plainLanguage: The dot5 MIB gives network-management software standard names for Token Ring settings and readings. SNMP can use those names to inspect or control an interface.

sections.title: Tables and Identifiers
sections.content:
The module defines an 802.5 Interface Table, an 802.5 Statistics Table, and a Timer Table. A system has one interface-table entry and one statistics-table entry for each Token Ring interface.

The Timer Table is obsolete, but its definition remains for backward compatibility. The module also defines object identifiers for interface tests and Token Ring chip sets.
sections.plainLanguage: The main tables report interface settings and statistics. The timer table is obsolete, but remains defined so older tools can still recognize it.

sections.title: Connection to the General Interface MIB
sections.content:
With the older interfaces group, each Token Ring interface maps one-to-one to an interface in RFC 1213. The shared ifIndex identifies corresponding objects.

The RFC also clarifies how Token Ring interfaces fit the Interface MIB requirements in RFC 1573. These objects apply to interfaces whose type is iso88025-tokenRing(9). The interface address is a 6-octet MAC address in the canonical order defined by IEEE 802.1a.
sections.plainLanguage: A Token Ring interface uses the same interface index as its entry in the general MIB. The dot5 objects apply only to interfaces identified as IEEE 802.5 Token Ring.

sections.title: Interface State and Commands
sections.content:
The dot5Table has one entry for each Token Ring interface. Its objects include commands to open, reset, or close the interface; ring status and state; the result of the latest attempt to enter the ring; ring speed; the upstream neighbor's address; and functional addresses.

The dot5RingStatus value is a sum of applicable condition values and ranges from 0 through 262143. The value 131072 means no status is available because opening has not completed. dot5RingSpeed describes the speed at the next insertion, which may differ from the current speed.
sections.plainLanguage: The interface table reports whether the station is in the ring and why an attempt to enter may have failed. It also provides commands to open, reset, or close the interface.

sections.title: Statistics and Error Counters
sections.content:
The dot5StatsTable has an entry for each interface and contains 18 Counter32 statistics. They count events defined by IEEE 802.5, including line errors, burst errors, abort transmissions, receive congestion, signal loss, and transmitted beacons.

Counter32 values wrap after their range is reached. If hardware maintains a statistic as a 16-bit counter, the SNMP agent must read it often enough to maintain the 32-bit value without losing counts.
sections.plainLanguage: The statistics table counts different Token Ring errors and events. The agent combines hardware readings often enough to keep each statistic as a 32-bit counter.

sections.title: Obsolete Timers and Interface Tests
sections.content:
The obsolete dot5TimerTable describes read-only timers in units of 100 microseconds. The RFC retains it only for backward compatibility.

Two test identifiers are defined: an Insert Function test and a Full-Duplex Loop Back test. The insert test can place the station on the network and may cause problems on an operational network. The module also identifies three Token Ring chip sets.
sections.plainLanguage: The old timer objects remain in the definition but are marked obsolete. The module also names two interface tests and three chip sets.

sections.title: Required Objects and Changes
sections.content:
An SNMPv2 entity implementing this MIB MUST support the state group and the statistics group. Write access to dot5ActMonParticipate and dot5Functional is not required; an implementation may expose them as read-only.

Compared with RFC 1231, RFC 1748 uses the SNMPv2 SMI, clarifies the relationship between its commands and interface status, adds dot5LastBeaconSent, and marks the timer table obsolete. Its security section says security issues are not discussed.
sections.plainLanguage: Every implementation must provide the state and statistics groups. The update adds a beacon timestamp and makes write access optional for two objects.
